name: Should an ADU kitchen have a dishwasher?

mainEntity.name: Is a dishwasher worth adding to a small ADU kitchen, or does it waste too much space?
mainEntity.text: Is a dishwasher worth adding to a small ADU kitchen, or does it waste too much space?

acceptedAnswer.text: A dishwasher can be a strong upgrade in an ADU kitchen, but only if the layout can support it without sacrificing the essentials. In a small footprint, cabinet storage and prep space may be more valuable than a full-size dishwasher, especially if the ADU is intended for occasional use or a single occupant. For a rental-oriented unit or a high-end guest suite, however, a dishwasher can make the kitchen feel much more complete and marketable. Compact dishwashers are often a smart compromise because they preserve more usable cabinet space while still adding convenience. The best decision depends on the lifestyle the unit is meant to support, the available plumbing and electrical routing, and how much daily cooking is expected. It also depends on whether the kitchen already feels tight; a dishwasher should not force awkward traffic patterns or block nearby drawers. In many cases, the best answer is a compact dishwasher only when the kitchen can absorb it naturally.
acceptedAnswer.description: A dishwasher is optional in many ADU kitchens, but it can improve rental appeal and convenience if the layout has room for it. In very small kitchens, a dishwasher may be less valuable than extra storage, counter space, or easier circulation. The right choice depends on the target use.
